answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-slash reputation grove: each agent locks tokens to join, and its record grows like a juniper tree, slow and visible. Fake identities cost real stake per copy, so spawning thousands drains the attacker. A pigment-style fingerprint, a hash of hardware, behavior, and past attestations, makes clones detectable; if one identity misbehaves, its whole grove of linked accounts loses its stake. Attackers pay per fake and risk losing everything, while honest agents keep cheap access.
